schedule.direction: Unchanged original summer daylight and sparse mature grass.
Afternoon: sun slightly lower toward camera-right than master, shadows slightly longer. Canopy90% green/10% muted yellow; lawn subtly less green than master, a few fallen leaves. NO sunset pink yet.

Late afternoon: camera-right sun lower again, shadows somewhat longer/softer. Canopy65% green/35% amber/russet. Moderate scattered leaves; grass slightly drier olive than previous stage. Sky pale blue, only very subtle warm wisps.

Golden evening: low camera-right sun, long softened shadows. Canopy35% green/65% red/russet/gold, retain a little green; slightly thinner than turning-leaves. Grass olive/dormant with moss only in existing shaded patches and moderate fallen leaves, NOT a uniform lush carpet. Warm sky restrained, no exaggerated sunset.

Sunset: very low camera-right sun almost gone, weak long shadows blending into diffuse skylight. IMPORTANT reduce existing leaf density by about HALF relative to autumn; many existing branches newly visible, remaining leaves muted brown/russet, not full dense red canopy. Fine frost and tiny snow traces on shaded5% of lawn/roof. Mostly damp dormant brown/olive grass with leaf litter. No spotlighting.

After sunset: diffuse cool sky, practically no direct sun and NO crisp sunny lawn patches. Existing branches mostly bare with a few brown leaves. Thin snow covers about40% of lawn and roof in coherent connected patches, not uniformly dusting every surface; exposed60% is dormant brown/olive grass. Snow begins in far-right shaded rise and left/below-deck shade, retaining exposed middle/foreground. Cool sky with faint peach at horizon.

Winter blue hour: soft diffuse cool light only, NO direct sunlight, NO hard white solar spot on red grill. Snow blanket covers about85% lawn and roof; preserve tiny dormant-grass margins in exposed foreground/near path so the next thaw does not reveal an entirely new lawn. Bare branches, minimal snow tracery rather than giant branch clumps. Clearly legible house and snow, not dark night. Golden cozy winter character will be restored in finishing; lamps off in this base image.

Very early dawn: diffuse blue-peach sky, no hard direct solar patches yet. Thaw: snow still covers about60% lawn/roof, SAME patches as winter shrinking from exposed middle/foreground toward far-right rise and below-deck shade. Exposed40% is mostly damp STRAW-BROWN / muted OLIVE dormant grass, not bright green. Bare branches with tiny buds. Slightly brighter than winter, no orange porch glow in base.

Sunrise: weak low sun from camera-left, very soft elongated shadows extending generally rightward; warm highlights only where reachable, no hard noon-white grill highlight. Snow still covers about30% lawn/roof, shrinking SAME shaded patches as snowmelt, especially far-right rise and below-deck shade. Newly exposed grass predominantly subdued straw/olive with small muted-green shoots; do NOT jump to lush spring green. Sparse buds/leaves on about20% existing canopy, majority branches still visible.

Early spring golden morning: low camera-left sun, soft long shadows consistent across house/yard/grill, not a copy of summer noon shadows. Last5% snow only tiny deep-shade remnants, no large banks. Lawn now predominantly muted fresh green but still mixed olive/straw, short growth, modest fine dew; NOT the old uniformly lush bright lime lawn. Fresh leaves about55% canopy density with existing branches visible. Preserve inviting morning character without a giant brightness jump.

Later spring, rising morning sun: direct light stronger, camera-left toward overhead, shorter softer shadows than spring. Snow fully gone. Lawn noticeably fuller soft green than early spring, but mixed natural patches and original terrain, not artificial turf; dew mostly evaporated. Canopy85% fresh green, naturally full. Red grill enamel highlight small/modest, light direction consistent, not chrome.

Late morning summer: sun approaches original master light direction/elevation, shadows and grill reflections nearly converge to master without jumping. Canopy mature deep green, full. Lawn begins drying back: mix mature green and original sparse/olive patches, between lush late spring and original late summer. Sky nearly master blue. No warm interior or exterior lamps in base.
